readme_featured_note: Ordered as one argument about AI and human coordination: why a race to be more, or above all others, cannot come to rest; why each counting only its own draw can together end what all depend on, the winner included; what anything that wants to go on must count, and where that stops; why selection and policy through a selector's couplings are blind to what does not couple in, including how far off the break is; why reforming the state without changing the rule is re-absorbed; why what cannot be undone cannot be tested by trial; what closing and opening the future exactly take; and why relations and wholes go on only through joint action and continuing generation. Each is checked in Lean on the pure core, whose source declarations have empty axiom reports; that is a constructive discipline, not an absence of premises, and each holds under the hypotheses its record states. Where a result says that something can happen, a constructed example shows that it can, not how often it does. None is new mathematics: each is near-definitional or a known result in the theory's vocabulary (the commons and overshoot, ranking-function termination, transitive closure, the proxy problem, Price's selection differential, opportunity-set inclusion), and the chapter's [relation to known results](theories/becoming/chapters/THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md#relation-to-known-results) names the closest prior result of each; what the work adds is that they are stated in one model with every premise named. Chosen for significance; the selection is open to revision.

site.note: The reader's site (tools/publishing/build_site.py): pages is the allow-list, nothing else is published; a path the push screen keeps private, or under sources/, is refused. nav and ways_in are AI-written navigation and name only pages listed here. The Pages job (.github/workflows/pages.yml) runs only when dispatched; enabling Pages is Ren's. With site.map on, the connection map is written as connections.html by connection_map's site mode. A card's time says what it is of; its fields are computed by the builder (card_time). chapters get contents and previous and next links. rewrites change the site's text only: two experiment READMEs print a local path and review receipts bind their hash, so they are redacted at build; words true only off the site are dropped there; the Chinese crosswalk, a generated page, is given a link to the map under its title. The opening's card times the text README's first screen times as {{time:opening}} ({body}), so the two agree.
site.title: The Theory of Becoming
site.description: One account of how things form, persist, change and end, with Lean-checked models and frozen tests; it asserts no should, and ranks courses only under two readings it names: the continuation condition (scope) and C, widening what can form is better (order).

notes._process/research/2026-10-05-generative-: The study was one bilingual file until 17 October 2026, when it was split. Most of the prose of sections 1–162 went to the Chinese edition (108 kept an English heading). The English file kept their anchors, code blocks and some tables, under no heading, on the pages marked so here, and in some sections lines the Chinese edition lacks, among them quoted words in English; its English summary gives an English account of some of these sections. Sections 163–165 each have an English account on their own pages. The Chinese edition's banner says that where the two differ the English governs. Records bind the English file by hash, at the version each read; none binds the Chinese edition or a page here. Their histories name sections by number.
